# Your first swarm

Goal: two agents editing one repo, zero checkouts, one prevented
conflict.

## Setup

```sh
git init demo && cd demo
git commit -qm init --allow-empty
sturn init
sturn daemon &            # or: sturn deploy service
```

## Two workspaces

```sh
sturn ws new agent-a
sturn ws new agent-b
```

Both point at `HEAD`. Nothing was written to disk — no worktree,
no index, no checkout.

## Claim before you edit

```sh
STURN_ACTOR=agent-a sturn claim "src/**" --ws agent-a
# claimed src/** (ws agent-a, ttl 3600s)

STURN_ACTOR=agent-b sturn claim "src/lib.rs" --ws agent-b
# conflict: agent-a claimed src/** (ws agent-a, expires …)
# sturn: claim denied — --force to override
```

Agent-b learns in milliseconds that `src/` is taken and picks
`tests/**` instead. In git, both would have edited the file and
discovered it at merge.

## Write ops, snap, repeat

```sh
echo '…' | sturn write src/lib.rs --ws agent-a
echo '…' | sturn write tests/lib.rs --ws agent-b
sturn snap agent-a -m "a: lib"   # → real commit on main
sturn snap agent-b -m "b: test"  # → real commit on main
```

`git log` shows two ordinary signed-able commits. `git for-each-ref
refs/sturn/*` shows the coordination layer GitHub never needed to
understand.

---

---
url: /sturn/how-to/hydrate.md
---
# Hydrate a workspace

Agents read through the ODB; compilers need POSIX files. Hydration
materializes the ws *view* — tip commit **plus** uncommitted WAL
ops, matching what `ws_read` sees.

```sh
sturn ws hydrate agent-7 /tmp/ws-7            # whole view
sturn ws hydrate agent-7 /tmp/ws-7 --path src # subset
```

Or hydrate + run + clean in one step:

```sh
sturn exec --ws agent-7 -- cargo check        # tmpfs, gone after
sturn exec --ws agent-7 --keep -- cargo test  # keep the dir
```

* Target tmpfs (`/dev/shm`/`/tmp`) — it's a projection, delete freely.
* Exit status propagates: `sturn exec` fails iff the command does.
* Writes inside the hydrated dir do **not** flow back — ops are the
  only write path. (Write-back hydration is a backlog item.)
* FUSE mounts for humans land last — `git` works meanwhile.

---

---
url: /sturn/how-to/daemon.md
---
# Run the daemon

`sturn daemon` polls WAL heads and fans new events onto topics
(`repo.<id>.ops|claims|review|presence`) in the embedded bus store.

```sh
sturn daemon                      # foreground
sturn deploy service              # systemd user unit, Restart=always
```

## If the daemon is down

Nothing is lost. The bus is a cache — ops still live in
`refs/sturn/wal/*` and replicate via `git push`/`git fetch`.
Subscribers catch up by replaying the WAL. The daemon only removes
latency; it never owns truth.

## Consumers today

* `sturn claims` — fold all WALs into live advisory locks
* M2: SSE/unix-socket subscribers; M3: the MCP `subs` tool

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/architecture.md
---
# Architecture

Three layers, strictly ordered by authority:

```
        ┌────────── evented layer ──────────┐
agents  │  ops: write/rename/claim/intent/… │
        │  virtual workspaces (ws = pointer) │
        │  bus: repo.<id>.{ops,claims,…}     │
        └──────┬─────────────────┬───────────┘
               │ append          │ append (offline)
        refs/sturn/wal/* ── git ODB ── refs/sturn/ws/*
               │
        normal git push/fetch → GitHub — free, signed, ordinary
```

## Invariants

1. **The WAL is the state.** Anything derivable from
   `refs/sturn/wal/*` is a cache (bus cursors, materialized views).
2. **Merges stay git's.** Ops never encode merge semantics — claims
   prevent collisions; `snap` squashes into ordinary commits.
3. **Coordination before work.** Claims publish *before* edits.
   Discovering a conflict at merge is the failure mode git taught us.

## What each piece owes

* `refs/sturn/wal/<ws>` — source of truth, replicates for free
* daemon + bus — latency reduction only; optional
* `refs/sturn/ws/<name>` — workspace namespaces; hydration opt-in
* `snap` — the bridge back to ordinary git history

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/no-crdt.md
---
# Why no CRDT for code

CRDTs are right for the *log*, wrong for the *tree*.

**For the WAL:** when replicas append ops and diverge, a CRDT-style
merge (grow-only set + causal order) converges the log with no
coordination — same events, same state. That part we keep.

**For the tree:** a CRDT auto-merge produces a *syntactically*
merged file, not a semantically correct one. Two agents inserting
different `main()` bodies converge to a file that compiles only by
luck. Code needs decisions, not convergence.

So sturn splits the difference:

* The **log** merges deterministically (CRDT semantics; a
  `libgrite-git` impl is on the backlog).
* The **tree** is produced by `snap` — a deterministic reduction
  over ops on a base. When ops collide semantically, that's a
  decision for a reviewer, not a merge algorithm.
* **Claims** make most collisions never happen — prevention beats
  resolution.

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/model.md
---
# The model — files, approval, agents

## Files are a projection, not the state

Git materializes a working tree because POSIX tools need paths.
Sturn keeps the tree *virtual*: `ws_read` serves blob contents
straight from the object database — no checkout, no index, no lock.

When something genuinely needs real files:

* `sturn exec --ws w -- cmd` — hydrate the ws view (tip +
  uncommitted ops) to tmpfs, run, discard
* `sturn mount w /dir --rw` — live FUSE filesystem; edits buffer
  per-open and become Write/Delete/Rename ops on release
* `--writeback` on `exec`/`hydrate` — dir diffs flow back as ops

Agents aren't filesystem-deprived — `ws_read/ws_write/ws_glob/
ws_grep` are the same file primitives harnesses already use; the
backend is virtualized, not the interaction.

## Approval without the PR cliff

Every op is content-addressed and streams through the WAL. A
reviewer emits `review <op-id> approve|reject` — itself a signed,
attributed op. With `[review] require = true`, `snap` refuses
unreviewed tree ops and names their ids — the gate exists, but
verdicts stream *per-op before commit time* instead of one giant
diff at the end. PRs become a packaging format, not the gate.

## Agents review agents

A verdict is just an op — any actor appends it. Intended topology:
fast writers produce ops → a senior agent or human watches `subs
ops|review` and emits verdicts → gated `snap` lands only approved
work. Humans spot-check the stream instead of serializing merges.

---

---
url: /sturn/reference/ops.md
---
# Ops

The event vocabulary appended to `refs/sturn/wal/<ws>`. JSON,
content-addressed (blob sha = event id), one commit per append.

## Tree ops

| Op | Fields | Effect at `snap` |
|---|---|---|
| `write` | `path`, `blob`, `intent?` | replace/create file |
| `rename` | `from`, `to` | move entry |
| `delete` | `path` | remove entry |

## Coordination ops

| Op | Fields | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | `glob`, `ttl_secs` | advisory lock; auto-expires |
| `release` | `glob` | drop a claim |
| `intent` | `text` | provenance — why the work exists |
| `review` | `event`, `verdict` | approve/reject an event id |
| `snapshot` | `message` | marker — ops before it are committed |
| `presence` | `status` | actor joined/left |

## Envelope

```json
{"id":"<blob sha>","ws":"agent-7","actor":"agent-7","ts":1792292994,
 "op":{"op":"write","path":"src/lib.rs","blob":"<sha>","intent":"…"}}
```

---
url: /sturn/reference/cli.md
---
# CLI reference

Global flags: `--repo <dir>` (default cwd) · `--config <path>`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sturn init` | write `sturn.toml`; confirm ref namespaces |
| `sturn ws new <name> [--base]` | create workspace ref — no checkout |
| `sturn ws ls` | list workspaces |
| `sturn ws read <ws> <path>` | blob contents, straight from the ODB |
| `sturn ws hydrate <ws> <dir> [--path P] [--writeback]` | materialize view; --writeback diffs dir → ops |
| `sturn claim <glob> --ws <w> [--ttl N] [--force]` | advisory lock; exits 1 on live conflict |
| `sturn release <glob> --ws <w>` | drop a claim |
| `sturn claims` | live claims across every workspace |
| `sturn write <path> --ws <w> [--file F] [--intent T]` | append a write op (stdin → blob) |
| `sturn intent <text> --ws <w>` | record provenance |
| `sturn log [--ws <w>]` | replay the WAL as JSONL |
| `sturn snap <ws…> -m <msg>` | fold ops → commit; multi-ws merges into one |
| `sturn review <event-id> <approve\|reject> --ws <w>` | continuous review |
| `sturn push [--remote R]` | push heads + `refs/sturn/*` |
| `sturn daemon` | WAL → topic fan-out loop + `bus.sock` push |
| `sturn sub <topic>` | stream ops|claims|review|presence as JSONL |
| `sturn mcp [--ws W]` | MCP stdio server; --ws emits joined/left presence |
| `sturn exec --ws <w> [--keep][--writeback] -- cmd…` | hydrate → run → clean; write-back as ops |
| `sturn join\|leave <ws>` | presence; leave sweeps actor claims |
| `sturn rename\|delete … --ws` | tree ops that keep intent |
| `sturn verify [--ws W]` | verify event sigs vs allowed_signers |
| `sturn compact [--ws W]` | drop pre-snapshot WAL history (archived) |
| `sturn bridge --to <url>` | snapshot ops → HMAC webhook (bupha CI) |
| `sturn mount <ws> <dir> [--rw]` | FUSE mount; --rw edits flow back as ops |
| `sturn deploy service\|env` | systemd unit / secrets skeleton |

# Config reference

`sturn.toml` — searched at `$STURN_CONFIG`, `./sturn.toml`,
`~/.config/sturn/sturn.toml`. Unknown fields are rejected. Secrets
never live here.

```toml
[repo]
dir = "."              # required — the git repo being coordinated
id = "9aia/sturn"      # topic prefix; default: dir basename
branch = "main"        # snap target; default: main

[wal]
ref_prefix = "refs/sturn/wal"   # default

[bus]
store = "~/.local/state/sturn/bus.redb"   # default
poll_ms = 100                             # daemon fan-out interval
# repos = ["../other-repo"]             # extra repos to fan out

[review]
require = true         # snap refuses unreviewed tree ops

[signing]
key = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"             # sign every event (ssh-keygen)
# allowed_signers = "..."

[actor]
name = "agent-7"       # default: $STURN_ACTOR → $USER → "anon"
```

See `examples/sturn.toml.example` in the repo.

url: /sturn/reference/crate-api.md
---
# Crate map

Ports (traits only) and impls — new backends are new impl crates,
never core changes.

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `sturn-core` | `Event`/`Op`/`Verdict`, `Config`, topic names |
| `sturn-wal` → `sturn-wal-git` | append-only op log in git refs (CAS) |
| `sturn-bus` → `sturn-bus-redb` | topic pub/sub cache over the WAL |
| `sturn-ws` → `sturn-ws-git` | virtual workspaces over the ODB |
| `sturn-vcs` → `sturn-git` | remote sync/push; `snap_commit` bridge |
| `sturn-claim` | pure claim logic: fold → live locks → conflicts |
| `sturn-mcp` | the agent tool contract (M3 wires the server) |
| `sturn-config` → `sturn-config-toml` | config source |
| `sturn-secret` → `sturn-keyring`/`sturn-dotenv` | secret resolution |
| `sturn-service` → `sturn-systemd` | daemon lifecycle |
| `sturn-cli` | `sturn` binary — the composition root |

Rustdoc: `/api/sturn_core/` etc. after `bun run docs:api`.

---
url: /sturn/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/sturn sturn
cd your-repo
sturn init
```

`init` writes a `sturn.toml` and confirms the ref namespaces. From
here, workspaces are the unit of parallel work:

```sh
sturn ws new agent-7      # refs/sturn/ws/agent-7 → HEAD. No checkout.
sturn ws ls
```

Append ops to the workspace's log:

```sh
echo 'fn helper() { 42 }' | sturn write src/lib.rs --ws agent-7 --intent "add helper"
sturn claim "src/**" --ws agent-7
sturn log --ws agent-7    # JSONL replay of the WAL
```

Land the work as an ordinary commit:

```sh
sturn snap agent-7 -m "add helper"   # ops → real commit on main
sturn push                           # heads + refs/sturn/* → origin
```

Run the coordination daemon so other actors see ops live:

```sh
sturn daemon             # WAL → repo.<id>.{ops,claims,review,presence}
sturn deploy service     # systemd user unit
```

Next: [your first swarm](/tutorials/first-swarm).
